1. Recall that we [showed that $\zeta(z)=\eta(z)/(1-2^{1-z})$](../../notes/QuasiRiemann/#zeta-eta). I've also stated (without proof) a couple of times that
$$
\zeta(2) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^2} = \frac{\pi^2}{6}
\text{ and }
\zeta(4) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^4} = \frac{\pi^4}{90}.
$$
Use those facts to find closed-form expressions for 
$$
\eta(2) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n^2}
\text{ and }
\eta(4) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n^4}.
$$

2. Use the definition of the exponential function to show that

   a. $|e^z| \leq e^{|z|}$
   b. $\displaystyle \lim_{z\to0} \frac{e^z-1}{z} = 1$

3. Compute the values of the following:

   a. $\text{Log}(\sqrt{3}+i)$
   b. $\log(8i)$
   c. $(1+i)^{\pi i}$
   d. $2^i$
